content.value_statement: ML teams need reproducible workflows that connect data preparation, training, validation, deployment, and monitoring. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through practical MLOps pipeline design and rollout decisions.
actual_capabilities: Designs stage-based ML pipelines from data ingestion through model deployment.
Explains orchestration patterns for Airflow, Dagster, Kubeflow Pipelines, and Prefect.
Covers data validation, feature engineering, data versioning, and lineage practices.
Guides model training workflows with experiment tracking and hyperparameter management.
Describes validation gates, baseline comparisons, A/B testing, and rollback planning.
Outlines deployment strategies such as shadow, canary, and blue-green releases.
limitations: Provides workflow guidance and examples, not a runnable pipeline generator.
Does not validate live data, train models, or deploy infrastructure by itself.
Requires project-specific tool choices, cloud permissions, and security controls.
Does not replace review by data science, platform, and compliance owners.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Training Pipeline
use_cases.description: Map the required stages, dependencies, validation gates, and ownership model before implementation starts.

use_cases.title: Standardize MLOps Practices
use_cases.description: Create team guidance for data versioning, experiment tracking, deployment rollouts, and production monitoring.

use_cases.title: Review Production Readiness
use_cases.description: Check whether a model workflow includes testing, rollback paths, observability, and performance regression controls.

prompt_templates.title: Outline a Basic Pipeline
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a simple model workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to outline a basic ML pipeline for my project. Include data preparation, training, validation, deployment, and monitoring stages.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an Orchestrator
prompt_templates.scenario: Compare workflow tools for a team decision.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to compare Airflow, Dagster, Kubeflow Pipelines, and Prefect for our ML workflow. Recommend an option based on our constraints.

prompt_templates.title: Design Validation Gates
prompt_templates.scenario: Add quality controls before model release.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design validation gates for a production model. Cover data checks, model metrics, baseline comparison, and approval criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Advanced MLOps Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of a production workflow with rollout controls.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review our end-to-end MLOps workflow. Identify gaps in orchestration, experiment tracking, canary deployment, rollback, and drift monitoring.

output_examples.input: Create a first version of an ML pipeline for a churn prediction model.
output: A staged workflow covering ingestion, validation, feature engineering, training, evaluation, deployment, and monitoring.
A dependency map that separates data readiness, model approval, and serving rollout tasks.
A short checklist for logs, metrics, ownership, and rollback readiness.

output_examples.input: Help decide whether our team should use Airflow or Kubeflow Pipelines.
output: A comparison based on infrastructure, Kubernetes usage, ML artifact tracking, team skills, and operational support.
A recommendation with tradeoffs and migration considerations.
Questions to confirm before committing to the orchestration platform.

output_examples.input: Review our model deployment plan before launch.
output: A readiness review covering baseline metrics, canary rollout, monitoring, alerts, and rollback triggers.
A list of missing controls that could delay or block release.
Suggested next steps for production validation and post-launch monitoring.

best_practices: Define stage inputs, outputs, ownership, and failure behavior before choosing tools.
Version data, code, model artifacts, and configuration for every training run.
Use validation gates and gradual rollout strategies before serving new models to all traffic.
anti_patterns: Deploying a model without baseline comparison, monitoring, or rollback criteria.
Mixing training, validation, and serving concerns in one untestable workflow step.
Treating orchestration as a substitute for data quality checks and experiment tracking.

faq.question: Does this skill generate production-ready code?
faq.answer: No. It provides architecture guidance, workflow patterns, and review checklists for ML pipeline implementation.

faq.question: Which orchestration tools does it discuss?
faq.answer: It covers Airflow, Dagster, Kubeflow Pipelines, and Prefect as common orchestration options.

faq.question: Can it help with data validation?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for data quality checks, feature engineering, versioning, and lineage tracking.

faq.question: Does it cover model deployment?
faq.answer: Yes. It discusses serving patterns, canary releases, blue-green deployments, rollback, and monitoring.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: ML engineers, platform engineers, and data science leaders can use it to plan and review MLOps workflows.

faq.question: Does it require a specific cloud provider?
faq.answer: No. It references AWS SageMaker, Google Vertex AI, Azure ML, and Kubernetes-based serving options.
